data.text: The N+1 problem is the most common performance issue in GraphQL. DataLoader batches and caches data fetches so you make one query instead of N+1.
When a query fetches a list of books and then resolves the author for each book, you execute one query for books plus N queries for authors.

data.caption: N+1 query pattern vs DataLoader batching.
data.definition:
graph TB
    A[N+1 Pattern] --> B[1 query: Get Books]
    B --> C[N queries: Get Author per Book]
    C --> D[Total: N+1 queries]

    E[DataLoader] --> F[1 query: Get Books]
    F --> G[1 batched query: Get Authors by IDs]
    G --> H[Total: 2 queries]

Caching
data.text: DataLoader caches results within a single request. If the same author ID is requested multiple times, only one database call is made.

terms.definition: Executing one query for a list and then N additional queries for each item's relation.
A pattern that batches and caches data fetches to avoid the N+1 problem.

data.description: Build a GenreBatchLoader that loads multiple genres by ID in one database call, then use it in a resolver.
steps: Create GenreBatchLoader inheriting from BatchDataLoader<int, Genre>
Load genres by IDs in LoadBatchAsync
Inject GenreBatchLoader into a Book resolver
Return the genre for the book's GenreId
data.expectedOutcome: Querying multiple books' genres now uses a single batch query instead of one query per book.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: DataLoader batches multiple loads into one query
Results are cached within a request
Solve N+1 at the resolver level
